before.lead: A group admission threshold does not explain every part of an organized visit. I help Osage County attractions distinguish who qualifies for a group arrangement from any extra guided experience the organizer wants.
before.decisionTitle: Keep group admission and a guided visit as separate arrangements.
before.decision: Woolaroc’s group information states a minimum of twenty paying adults and describes complimentary admission for an escort and driver. It separately offers guided adult tours for an additional charge with two weeks’ notice. Those conditions answer different planning questions. For a business with similar choices, I would explain the separate count and service questions before the organizer contacts staff. The owner supplies and approves the operating facts; the website explains the choice and the next step.

scopes.title: Clarify the group request introduction
scopes.request: Count paying adults separately from the escort and driver, decide whether you want a guided visit, and check the notice requirement before contacting staff.
scopes.supplies: Current group thresholds, complimentary-role rules, guide charge and notice wording.
scopes.check: A party with eighteen paying adults plus an escort and driver is not described as meeting a twenty-paying-adult threshold.

scopes.title: Build an organized-visit section
scopes.request: Describe your group’s admission needs and whether you want a guided visit, then ask staff about the applicable arrangements, notice and additional charge.
scopes.supplies: Approved visit descriptions, group terms, guide arrangements and booking contact.
scopes.check: A group meeting the admission threshold still receives a separate explanation of guide availability, notice and additional charge.

before.scopeTrigger: A group-information update can distinguish admission count from guide arrangements. A fuller organized-visit section is useful when organizers need to compare admission and interpretation before requesting a date. Any new booking, payment or automated approval functions need separate assessment.
quoteQuestions: Which participants count toward the group minimum?
Is a guide included or arranged separately?
Which lead time applies to the guided option?
before.coverageNote: Wonder and Method works online from Buffalo, New York, with Osage County businesses. The the Barnsdall vicinity example is public planning material, not a client, partner or endorsement.
